experiences.name: Cotefablo to Aínsa
experiences.description: From Biescas over the Cotefablo pass to Broto in the Ara valley below the Ordesa massif, then south along the Sobrarbe road to the walled square of Aínsa. Empty mountain tarmac, big limestone walls and a medieval finish.

experiences.name: Tramuntana: Andratx to Sa Calobra
experiences.description: The whole Serra de Tramuntana on the Ma-10 coast road: Valldemossa, Deià and Sóller, then over Puig Major to the Sa Calobra descent with its tied-knot hairpin. The best-known bend sequence in Mallorca; go early to avoid the coaches.

experiences.name: Rioja Wine Road
experiences.description: Haro, the home of the old bodegas, to Logroño by way of the hilltop walls of Laguardia and the vineyards of Rioja Alavesa. Easy, fast and pretty, with plenty of cellar doors for a stop.

experiences.name: Guadarrama: Navacerrada, Cotos and Morcuera
experiences.description: Three passes of the Sierra de Guadarrama in one short run: Navacerrada, Cotos and the Morcuera. Madrid's own mountain road, with pine forest, long views of the meseta and good bends all the way.

experiences.name: Teide Crossing
experiences.description: Across Tenerife on the TF-21: from the banana terraces of Puerto de la Cruz up through the pine forest into the Las Cañadas caldera, past the foot of the volcano and down to the south coast via Vilaflor. Lunar landscape at 2,000 m and a climate change on every side.

experiences.name: Ribeira Sacra Canyons
experiences.description: Galicia's hidden canyon country: the road follows the Sil gorge from Ourense past the Santo Estevo monastery to Parada de Sil, with terraced vineyards dropping straight into the river, and ends in Monforte de Lemos. Slow, twisty and quiet.

via.name: Santo Estevo de Ribas de Sil

experiences.name: Tarragona to Poblet via Prades
experiences.description: From the Roman coast of Tarragona through Reus and up into the Prades mountains, on to the Cistercian monastery of Poblet and the walled town of Montblanc. A mix of culture and wine country on quiet Catalan back roads.

experiences.name: Cabo de Gata Desert Coast
experiences.description: Through the Níjar badlands and the old gold-mining village of Rodalquilar to San José, on the quiet tarmac of Europe's only semi-desert coast. Dry volcanic hills, white villages and big sea views. A graded track continues from San José to the Genoveses and Mónsul beaches, but it is not part of this route.

experiences.name: San Glorio to the Beyos Gorge
experiences.description: Over the San Glorio pass from Potes to Riaño and then the Pontón pass and the dramatic Beyos gorge down to Cangas de Onís. A classic high-mountain crossing of the Picos de Europa with very little traffic.

experiences.name: Basque Coast Road
experiences.description: Bilbao to San Sebastián along the Bay of Biscay: Bermeo, Lekeitio and Zumaia with their fishing harbours, the flysch cliffs and the green coastal ridges. Short hops between villages and lots of stops for pintxos.

experiences.name: Vielha to La Seu over the Bonaigua
experiences.description: From the Val d'Aran over the Port de la Bonaigua at 2,072 m, down through Esterri d'Àneu and Sort, to La Seu d'Urgell. One of the highest passes in the Catalan Pyrenees, with generous hairpins on both sides.

experiences.name: White Villages: Ronda to Arcos
experiences.description: Ronda's gorge to Setenil's rock-roofed streets, then Zahara and Grazalema in the Sierra de Grazalema and down to the clifftop town of Arcos. Whitewashed villages, cork oaks and the Palomas pass in between.

experiences.name: Jerte Valley and Gredos
experiences.description: From Plasencia up the Jerte valley and over the Tornavacas pass, then along the northern side of the Sierra de Gredos through El Barco and Hoyos del Espino to Ávila. Wide mountain roads, cherry orchards in spring and granite peaks.

experiences.name: Castile Heritage: Toledo to Segovia
experiences.description: Three UNESCO cities in one day: Toledo, the complete walls of Ávila and the Roman aqueduct of Segovia, linked by the fast country roads of Castile. For culture and long straights rather than bends.

experiences.name: Costa Brava: Tossa to Cadaqués
experiences.description: The Catalan coast from Tossa de Mar and the twisty Sant Feliu road, via Begur and the Empordà plain, to Roses and the pass above Cadaqués. Coves and pine-covered cliffs, then a final bend-filled climb to Dalí's village.

experiences.name: Puerto de la Ragua
experiences.description: Over the Puerto de la Ragua (about 2,000 m), the highest paved road across the Sierra Nevada, from Laroles on the Alpujarra side to La Calahorra beneath its Renaissance castle. Short, quiet and exposed, with a long open descent on the northern side.

experiences.name: Andalusia Heritage: Seville to Granada
experiences.description: Seville's cathedral and Alcázar, the mosque-cathedral of Córdoba and the Alhambra of Granada, tied together by country roads through the Guadalquivir valley. A long, easy cultural run with olive groves on both sides; plan a full day.

experiences.name: Aragon to Aran: Jaca to Vielha
experiences.description: Across the central Pyrenees in one long day: Jaca, the Sobrarbe road to Aínsa, the Ribagorza valleys by Campo and El Pont de Suert, and up to Vielha in the Val d'Aran through the Vielha tunnel. Big valleys, limestone walls and very little traffic.

experiences.name: Cantabrian Coast: Santander to Cudillero
experiences.description: The green north coast through Llanes, Ribadesella and Gijón to the fishing village of Cudillero. Cliffs, beaches and the Picos de Europa seen from the sea, on coastal roads and a few faster stretches.

experiences.name: Maestrazgo: Tortosa to Teruel
experiences.description: From the Ebro delta town of Tortosa up through the Ports to Valderrobres and the walled town of Morella, then the empty Maestrazgo uplands via Cantavieja to Teruel. Long, quiet roads with very few villages.

experiences.name: Alpujarras: Granada to Almería
experiences.description: Granada to the Alpujarras: Lanjarón and Órgiva, then Capileira and Trevélez, the highest villages in Spain, and down across the Alpujarra Alta to Laujar and the coast at Almería. Whitewashed villages, hairpins and a change from alpine to desert.

experiences.name: Camino de Santiago: Pamplona to León
experiences.description: The Camino Francés by road: Pamplona, Logroño, Burgos and the meseta through Frómista and Sahagún to León. Romanesque churches and pilgrim hostels every few kilometres, long open horizons and a very long day in the saddle; best split in two.

experiences.name: Galician Atlantic Coast
experiences.description: A Coruña to Cambados by the Costa da Morte and the Rías Baixas: Muxía, then Cee at the foot of Cape Fisterra (the cape itself is a 15 km spur you can add), Muros and Ribeira. Granite headlands, lighthouses and seafood towns.

experiences.name: Santander to Cangas de Onís by the Picos
experiences.description: Out of Santander along the Cantabrian coast through Comillas and San Vicente de la Barquera, then inland to Panes and up the Cabrales valley to Arenas, home of the blue cheese, and on to Cangas de Onís at the foot of the Picos de Europa. Sea and cliffs first, then limestone walls.

experiences.name: Maestrat Back Roads: Culla to Lucena
experiences.description: Quiet Valencian highlands: from the hill town of Culla south through Atzeneta del Maestrat and Les Useres to Lucena del Cid, on empty local roads between the Alt Maestrat and the Alcalatén. Pine and holm oak, almost no traffic and a short, easy day; the sanctuary under Penyagolosa, the highest peak in Castellón, lies off this route to the west.
